holidays.name: Sadie Hawkins Day
holidays.description: Flip the script! This day celebrates the tradition of turning the tables on courtship. It's best known for dances where the ladies do the asking and the gents wait nervously by the punch bowl.
holidays.origin: It comes from Al Capp's classic comic strip Li'l Abner, which debuted in 1934. In the strip, homely Sadie Hawkins was so desperate for a husband that her father staged a footrace. Every unmarried woman in Dogpatch chased the town's bachelors, and any man she caught had to marry her. The idea took off with real-life schools and colleges, which started holding Sadie Hawkins dances in the late 1930s.
holidays.funFact: Sadie Hawkins events spread across hundreds of college campuses within just a few years of the comic's popularity, and the idea of a role-reversed dance still lives on in many high schools today.

holidays.name: National Indian Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to dig into a warm, spoon-friendly colonial classic: a baked pudding of cornmeal, milk, and molasses, spiced with ginger and cinnamon. It's often topped with a scoop of melting vanilla ice cream.
holidays.origin: Indian pudding grew out of early New England kitchens. Colonists adapted the English hasty pudding to the cornmeal they had on hand, which they called Indian meal, and sweetened it with molasses. It's an unofficial food observance, and the pudding has been a regional dessert staple for centuries.
holidays.funFact: Indian pudding is traditionally baked low and slow for hours, so the cornmeal turns silky and the molasses caramelizes into a deep, dark, spiced custard.

holidays.name: Symphonic Metal Day
holidays.description: Turn up the volume and cue the violins! This day salutes the music genre that marries thundering metal guitars and drums with sweeping orchestral arrangements, choirs, and operatic vocals.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin, created by fans of the genre. Symphonic metal grew out of the 1990s European metal scene, and bands like Nightwish, Within Temptation, and Epica helped make it popular.
holidays.funFact: Many symphonic metal bands record with full orchestras and choirs, so a single album can involve dozens of musicians on top of the usual guitars, bass, and drums.
